expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: export type Subscription = | (SubscriptionCore & { readonly status: "trialing"; ... }) | ... | discriminated by status field

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: Each union branch carries only its fields: trialing has trialEndsAt, canceled has canceledAt/cancellation, no overlap

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: export function assertNever(x: never): never... with default: return assertNever(sub) in hasAccess switch

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: type Brand<T, B extends string>; SubscriptionId, CustomerId, PlanId, RetryCount all branded

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: Provides function signatures (recoverPayment, exhaustRetries) with detailed business-logic questions; discriminated union constrains variants

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: Section titled 'What this leaves possible' lists what is NOT prevented (illegal transitions, stale dates, runtime boundary); does not explicitly enumerate which misuses ARE prevented by the design

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: Insight section: 'count the optional fields. {status, trialEndsAt?, retryCount?, ...} claims 2^6 = 64 legal states. Exactly 4 exist.' Recommends discriminated union
